envvars.noMatch: No documented variable matches these filters.
envvars.blockedBootstrap: Claude Code reads this before it loads settings, so a value here would leave one run resolving paths against two different directories. Set it in your shell instead.
envvars.blockedHostInjected: Injected per run by whatever launches Claude Code. A value written here is overwritten immediately.
envvars.noPreTrust: Not on Claude Code's pre-trust allowlist. No specific risk is documented for it.
envvars.providerManagedNote: A host-managed launch can override this regardless of what is set here.
envvars.legacyGlobalWins: Also set in ~/.claude.json, which Claude Code applies first. With no settings.json override, that value is what takes effect.
envvars.legacyGlobalShadowed: ~/.claude.json also sets this. Clearing here lets that value surface.
envvars.unsetHint: Remove the key — Claude Code decides
envvars.relaunchNote: Sessions already running keep the old value until you relaunch Claude Code.
envvars.clearBody: The key is removed from settings.json, so Claude Code's own default applies to new sessions. {{relaunch}}
envvars.notChanged: {{name}} was not changed — the field was no longer there.
envvars.secretConfirm: This writes the value into Claude Code's user settings file in plaintext. Claude Code does not encrypt it, and anything that can read the file can read the value.

hazardWarn.redirect: Changes where Claude Code sends traffic, or which traffic bypasses your proxy. Only use destinations and bypass rules you trust.
hazardWarn.trustCert: Changes which TLS certificates Claude Code trusts. A wrong value makes interception undetectable.
hazardWarn.executeCode: Names a binary, wrapper, or script that Claude Code runs. Only point it at local code you trust.
hazardWarn.switchProject: Switches which account or project your requests bill and log to.
hazardWarn.disableUpdates: Stops Claude Code from updating itself, including security fixes.

hazardConfirm.trustCert: This changes which TLS certificates are trusted.
hazardConfirm.executeCode: This value ends up in a command Claude Code runs.
hazardConfirm.switchProject: This changes which account or project you bill and log to.
hazardConfirm.disableUpdates: This stops Claude Code from updating itself.

envvars.unrecognizedNote: These keys are in your settings file but match no documented variable. Their values are not shown: an unrecognized name could be a credential. To see or change one, edit <path>{{path}}</path> by hand.
envvars.undocumentedNoneFound: Nothing undocumented was found in Claude Code {{version}}.
envvars.undocumentedFoundTitle: Documented nowhere — found in Claude Code {{version}} ({{total}})
envvars.undocumentedNote: These names were found by scanning your installed Claude Code binary. Anthropic does not document them. They can change or disappear in any release, their accepted values are unknown, and setting one carries no safety guarantee. Claudepot deliberately offers no control for them — guessing a type or a value would be worse than offering nothing. To set one anyway, edit <path>{{path}}</path> by hand.
envvars.undocumentedUnavailable: Unavailable — this list was built against Claude Code {{snapshot}} and you're running {{installed}}. These names can be renamed or removed in any release, so a list from a different version would be a guess rather than a finding.
envvars.versionUnresolved: a version Claudepot could not resolve

disclosure.editsBody: The env block of {{path}}. That path is resolved, not assumed — CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR moves it. Project-scoped settings are deliberately not editable here: Claude Code applies only its safe-variable allowlist from a project file, because those live inside the repository and could be committed by someone else.
disclosure.precedenceBody: In a normal CLI session Claude Code applies settings env after the launch environment, so it usually overrides your shell export. Managed, host-spawned and claude ssh contexts filter or supersede values. Whether an environment variable beats the matching settings field is per-variable, not a rule.
disclosure.legacyBody: ~/.claude.json carries its own env block, which Claude Code applies first — so this file wins where both set a key, and that one still takes effect where this file is silent. Rows it affects say so.
disclosure.effectBody: Claude Code re-applies settings env to a running session additively. Setting or changing a value is usually live. Clearing one never is — nothing is deleted from a running session's environment, so the old value survives until you relaunch Claude Code.
disclosure.unsetBody: Claude Code's default for nearly every variable is the key being absent, not a value. Restore default therefore removes the key; it never writes the documented default, which would pin today's number into your settings and override whatever Claude Code changes it to later. An explicit empty string is a third state again, distinct from both.
disclosure.snapshotFrom: Undocumented-name snapshot taken from Claude Code
disclosure.lifetimesNote: These are two separate facts with different lifetimes — the live documentation already lists variables absent from any given build — so neither date describes the other.

envvars.blockedEnvOnly: Claude Code reads this only from the environment you start `claude` from, never from a settings file. A value written here would be saved and then ignored. Set it in your shell instead.
